description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian classic known for its rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. This iconic dish features tender chicken pieces simmered in a velvety gravy infused with aromatic spices, butter, and cream. It is a comforting and flavorful meal perfect for any special occasion or a delightful weeknight dinner.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 min (optional)

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric powder, red chili powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken thoroughly. Cover and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until lightly browned and cooked through. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, reduce heat to medium and add the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the grated ginger and minced garlic, cooking for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Add the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews (if using), and water or chicken broth to the pan. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. If using cashews, this will also soften them for blending.

instructions.title: Blend and Refine the Sauce
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender (or use an immersion blender directly in the pot). Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Pass the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra silky texture, pressing down on any solids. Discard any remaining solids.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the seared chicken to the smooth sauce. Stir in the sugar and crushed Kasoori Methi. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the sauce's flavors. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and cook for another 2-3 minutes until heated through. Do not boil after adding cream.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot with naan bread, roti, or basmati rice. Enjoy your homemade classic Butter Chicken!

tips: For best flavor, marinate the chicken for at least 2 hours or overnight in the refrigerator. The longer it marinates, the more tender and flavorful the chicken will be.
If you want an extra rich and smooth sauce, blend the tomato and cashew mixture thoroughly until no lumps remain. Passing it through a sieve after blending ensures a restaurant-quality texture.
Always add the heavy cream at the very end and do not let the curry boil after adding it, as this can cause the cream to curdle. Just heat it through gently.
article:
Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani: The Quintessential Indian Delight

Few dishes evoke the rich tapestry of Indian cuisine quite like Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani. This iconic dish, with its creamy texture, vibrant color, and complex flavors, has captivated palates worldwide, cementing its place as a global favorite. Originating from the bustling kitchens of Delhi, Butter Chicken is more than just a meal; it's an experience – a harmonious blend of tender chicken, a luscious tomato-based sauce, and a symphony of aromatic spices. If you've ever yearned to recreate that restaurant-quality magic at home, you're in the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through the authentic Butter Chicken Recipe, ensuring a truly unforgettable culinary journey.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani (literally "chicken with butter"), is a classic Indian curry that originated in the 1950s at Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi. It was reportedly created by Kundan Lal Gujral, who also invented dal makhani and tandoori chicken. The dish was born out of a need to use leftover tandoori chicken, which he simmered in a rich tomato and butter gravy. The result was a revelation: a mild, subtly sweet, and incredibly rich curry that quickly became a sensation.

At its heart, Butter Chicken features marinated and grilled (or pan-fried) chicken pieces, traditionally tandoori chicken, swimming in a velvety smooth sauce. This sauce is a masterpiece of balance, typically made from tomatoes, fresh cream, butter, and a blend of spices that often includes ginger, garlic, garam masala, cumin, and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). Unlike many other Indian curries, Butter Chicken is not overly spicy, making it a beloved choice for those who appreciate nuanced flavors and a comforting, luxurious mouthfeel. Its distinct orange hue and signature swirl of cream are instantly recognizable, promising a delightful culinary adventure with every spoonful.

## Ingredients for Authentic Butter Chicken

Creating an authentic Butter Chicken Recipe requires attention to quality ingredients. Here's what you'll need:

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

**For the Makhani (Butter) Sauce:**
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter (plus more for finishing)
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1 (800g) can crushed tomatoes or 6-7 ripe medium tomatoes, blanched and pureed
*   1/2 cup cashews, soaked in hot water for 15-20 minutes (for creaminess)
*   1/2 cup water (or chicken broth)
*   1 tablespoon sugar (or to taste, to balance acidity)
*   1/2 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (plus more for garnish)
*   Salt to taste

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Butter Chicken

Embark on the journey to master the classic Butter Chicken Recipe with these detailed steps:

**1. Marinate the Chicken:**
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor and tenderness.

**2. Cook the Chicken:**
Heat a little oil in a large skillet or grill pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until lightly charred and cooked through. The charring adds a crucial smoky depth to the final dish. Set aside.

**3. Prepare the Makhani Sauce Base:**
In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 2 tablespoons of butter with 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent and softened, about 8-10 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

**4. Build the Flavor Profile:**
Add the red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, ground coriander, and ground cumin to the pot. Sauté for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until the spices are fragrant. Be careful not to burn them.

**5. Add Tomatoes and Cashews:**
Pour in the crushed tomatoes (or tomato puree). Add the soaked cashews and water/broth. Stir well, bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to break down.

**6. Create the Velvety Smooth Sauce:**
Carefully transfer the contents of the pot to a blender. Blend until absolutely smooth. For an extra silken texture, pass the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pot. This step is key for that restaurant-quality mouthfeel.

**7. Finish the Sauce:**
Return the pot to medium-low heat. Stir in the sugar, kasoori methi, and salt to taste. Bring to a gentle simmer. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Let it simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce.

**8. The Grand Finale:**
Remove the pot from heat. Stir in the heavy cream and a knob of fresh butter until melted and incorporated. Do not boil the sauce after adding the cream, as it can curdle. Taste and adjust seasonings if necessary. Your incredible Butter Chicken Recipe is almost ready!

## Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Achieving the perfect Butter Chicken isn't just about following a recipe; it's about understanding the nuances. Here are some pro tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, and the spices infuse deep flavor, which is crucial for the overall Butter Chicken Recipe.
*   **Charred Chicken:** While you don't need a tandoor, getting a good char on the chicken in a hot pan or grill adds a smoky depth that elevates the dish significantly.
*   **Quality Tomatoes:** Use good quality canned crushed tomatoes or very ripe fresh tomatoes. They form the backbone of the sauce.
*   **Soaked Cashews:** Cashews provide a natural sweetness and richness, contributing to the sauce's signature creaminess without relying solely on dairy. Don't skip soaking them for easier blending.
*   **Blend and Sieve:** For that incredibly smooth, restaurant-style sauce, always blend thoroughly and then pass it through a fine-mesh sieve. This removes any fibrous bits from onions or tomatoes.
*   **Kasoori Methi:** This dried fenugreek leaf is indispensable. It adds a unique, slightly bitter, and aromatic flavor that is characteristic of authentic Murgh Makhani. Gently crush it between your palms before adding to release its full aroma.
*   **Balance Sweetness and Acidity:** Tomatoes are acidic. Sugar helps balance this and enhances the overall flavor profile. Adjust to your preference.
*   **Don't Boil Cream:** Always add cream at the very end, off the heat, or just before serving, and never bring the sauce to a rolling boil after it's added, to prevent curdling.

## Serving Suggestions for Murgh Makhani

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs beautifully with a variety of accompaniments, creating a truly satisfying Indian feast.

*   **Naan Bread:** Soft, chewy naan, especially garlic naan or butter naan, is the quintessential pairing. It's perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich, buttery sauce.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Fluffy, aromatic basmati rice (plain or jeera rice with cumin seeds) provides a neutral canvas that allows the complex flavors of the Butter Chicken to shine.
*   **Raita:** A cooling side of cucumber raita (yogurt with grated cucumber and spices) offers a refreshing contrast to the richness of the curry.
*   **Pickle and Salad:** A simple side salad of sliced onions, cucumbers, and tomatoes, perhaps with a squeeze of lemon, along with some Indian pickle, can add a refreshing crunch and tangy kick.
*   **Garnish:** A swirl of fresh cream, a sprinkle of chopped fresh coriander leaves, or a few slivers of fresh ginger make for a beautiful and flavorful garnish.

## Variations & Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken Recipe is a masterpiece, there are ways to adapt it to dietary needs or personal preferences:

*   **Healthier Version:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream. You can substitute some of the cream with milk or even a plant-based alternative like cashew cream. For the chicken, ensure it's skinless and grilled.
*   **Vegan Butter "Chicken":** Replace chicken with firm tofu, paneer, or a plant-based chicken substitute. Use coconut cream or cashew cream instead of dairy cream, and a plant-based butter alternative.
*   **Spicier Kick:** If you prefer more heat, add a green chili or two, finely chopped, along with the ginger-garlic paste, or increase the amount of red chili powder.
*   **Different Proteins:** While chicken is traditional, this sauce base works wonderfully with other proteins. Try it with paneer (Paneer Makhani), shrimp, or even hard-boiled eggs for a delightful twist.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** For an authentic smoky taste without a tandoor, you can use the "dhungar" method: place a small bowl with a hot charcoal piece in the pot, drizzle a little ghee over it, and cover for a few minutes.

Butter Chicken is more than just a dish; it's a culinary hug, a symbol of comfort and exquisite flavor. With this detailed Butter Chicken Recipe, you now have all the tools and knowledge to recreate this beloved Indian classic in your own kitchen. Prepare to impress your family and friends with a meal that is truly rich, aromatic, and utterly unforgettable. Enjoy the journey of making and savoring this magnificent Murgh Makhani!
